definitions.explanation: The philosophical and ethical system based on the teachings of Confucius, emphasizing moral virtue, social harmony, filial piety, and proper conduct in relationships.

examples.japanese: {儒教|じゅきょう}の{教|おし}えを{学|まな}ぶ。
{儒教|じゅきょう}は{東|ひがし}アジアの{文化|ぶんか}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: Confucianism had a great influence on East Asian culture.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{日本|にほん}では{儒教|じゅきょう}が{武士|ぶし}の{道徳|どうとく}の{基盤|きばん}となっていた。
examples.english: In Edo-period Japan, Confucianism served as the moral foundation for the samurai class.

notes:
Confucianism was introduced to Japan from China and had a significant influence on Japanese society, particularly during the Edo period (1603-1868) when it was promoted by the Tokugawa shogunate. Core values include {仁|じん} (benevolence), {義|ぎ} (righteousness), {礼|れい} (propriety), and {孝|こう} (filial piety).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {儒教|じゅきょう}の{思想|しそう} (Confucian thought)
- {儒教|じゅきょう}の{影響|えいきょう} (influence of Confucianism)
- {儒教|じゅきょう}{的|てき}な{価値観|かちかん} (Confucian values)
